summary: Object-side (write-driven) binding-reconcile queue records (cinatra#1493, epic #1424). Extends artifact_binding_reconcile_queue so the write-path binding reconcile is crash-durable: a create into a claimed type, or a type-change AWAY from a claimed type, enqueues a per-artifact 'binding-reconcile-write' row in the SAME transaction as the object write (upsertObjectAndEnqueue), carrying the concrete (org_id, object_id) so the consumer reconciles exactly that artifact — the claim-side queue is winner-transition-driven and TYPE-swept and cannot select a row whose type already moved away from the claimed type. Adds two NULLABLE identity columns (object_id, org_id), relaxes claim_event_id to NULLABLE (a write-driven row has no claim event), widens the kind CHECK to admit 'binding-reconcile-write', and adds a shape CHECK keeping each kind's required columns honest (write rows require object_id+org_id; claim rows require claim_event_id — every existing row is claim-side and already satisfies it). Gate class NON-destructive (additive/loosening): nullable columns + a DROP NOT NULL + a CHECK that only ADMITS a new value + a CHECK no existing row violates — no NOT NULL on existing data, no unique index, no tightened constraint, no data rewrite. Mirrors the idempotent bootstrap DDL in src/lib/artifact-claim-schema.ts (artifactClaimSchemaQueries, spread into buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries) so fresh-bootstrap and operator-upgrade stay aligned (core__0034/core__0041 precedent). down() deletes still-pending write-driven rows (idempotently re-enqueued by the next affected write; the reconcile always resolves the live winner, so no binding permanently diverges), narrows the kind CHECK, restores claim_event_id NOT NULL, and drops the added columns. SEQ IS PROVISIONAL: assigned at merge; a concurrent S2-stream migration PR may also claim 0043 — renumber-at-merge is normal.
